task.title: Collapse the duplicated protected-login step classification onto its canonical set
task.objective: PROTECTED_LOGIN_STEP_TYPES is exported from src/profiles/FlowProfile.ts beside the StepType union that defines those names, but two private copies predate it: PROTECTED_LOGIN_STEP_TYPES in src/security/authz/AiAutonomyPolicy.ts and PROTECTED_STEP_TYPES in src/runner/evidence/FailureEvidenceCollector.ts. Replace both with imports of the canonical set. Only the first is Risk 3 and needs this lease; the other two files are ordinary paths. This is a de-duplication, not a policy change: membership stays exactly protectedLoginHandoff, autoSecureLogin and reuseSession, and no protected-login restriction is broadened or relaxed. The drift guard in verify:flow-fragments is retargeted at the consolidated wiring rather than deleted with the duplication it watched.

acceptance.description: AiAutonomyPolicy.ts no longer declares its own literal set of protected-login step types; it reads the canonical export, and the membership is unchanged.

The verify:flow-fragments drift guard still fails if a consumer stops agreeing with the canonical set — it asserts the consolidated wiring rather than being deleted along with the duplication it watched.

evidence.notes: tsc --noEmit plus all three bundles, run after both consumers were collapsed onto the canonical set.

103/103, up from 97 — §12 now asserts the consolidated wiring (each consumer imports the canonical set and declares no competing set literal, whatever it is named) plus the REAL behaviour of decideAiAction for every canonical member and a non-member negative control, instead of comparing three literals, which would now be one literal compared with itself. Mutation-tested: re-introducing the private literal set in FailureEvidenceCollector.ts failed exactly the competing-set check at 102/103, and the source was restored.
138/138, including the whole Protected Login Handoff and Auto Secure Login / Reuse Session sections that the collected evidence suppression governs.
62/62. This suite restates the ratified T3 table independently of the policy module, so it is the check that would catch the consolidation quietly changing what T3 forbids. It did not.

35/35. CORRECTED after independent QC: this suite drives FlowExecutor.executeWithRetry for FR-B2 per-attempt evidence and never mentions a protected step type or the suppression flag, so it is a regression check on the changed FILE, not evidence for the changed BEHAVIOUR. It should not be read as the latter.

85/85 through the real engine, including section 11 'A protected-login surface is excluded entirely' — nothing page-derived kept, exclusions counted rather than silent, no canary from the login surface in the report, and the next ordinary document in the same page captured again. This is the suite that exercises the suppression path the consolidation touches. It asserts exclusion by page/document canary rather than by step type, so it does not by itself pin the MEMBERSHIP of the set for this consumer — see the QC finding recorded on this contract.

qc_review.method: Independent awkit-qc-reviewer subagent, read-only, reviewing the working tree directly. NOTE: the lease guard gates shell on isRootPrimaryIdentity (tools/agents/lease-guard.mjs:450), so a subagent cannot run git or any verifier — the review is source-read only and could not read the pre-change literals from history. That limitation is itself a finding below.
findings: 1 (non-blocking, evidence gap): membership is identical at all three consumption sites — FlowProfile.ts:65-69 is the single literal, AiAutonomyPolicy.ts:92 and FailureEvidenceCollector.ts:83 are plain aliases of that same object, FlowFragment.ts:330 reads it directly. The reviewer could not independently corroborate the RUNNER consumer's PRE-change membership; verify-ai-autonomy-policy.mts:75 independently restates the security consumer's.

2 (no issue): the ReadonlySet<StepType> to ReadonlySet<string> widening is compile-time only. Set.prototype.has does not consult TypeScript types, both call sites already passed arbitrary strings (AiAutonomyPolicy.ts:186 reads context.step.type: string; FailureEvidenceCollector.ts:278 reads event.stepType ?? ""), so the matched values are byte-identical and the widening only removes a cast that would have lied about unchecked input.

3 (no issue): nothing broadened or weakened. T3 refusal is unchanged and still evaluated before configuration (AiAutonomyPolicy.ts:186-188); the fragment audit still emits protectedLoginStep for every member (FlowFragment.ts:329-337); evidence suppression still fires on a protected step and retracts the step page's document (FailureEvidenceCollector.ts:278-280), with the independent waitingForManualAction suppression at 262-267 untouched.

4 (no issue): no import cycle and no layering violation. src/profiles/FlowProfile.ts has zero import statements at all, so it is a leaf type/const module and cannot cycle back into src/security/**; AiAutonomyPolicy's documented purity claim at lines 23-24 stays true.

5 (non-blocking, ACTED ON in part): the retargeted guard is load-bearing in the four vacuity shapes checked, but the competing-copy scan matched only `new Set([...])` literals, so a copy written as an array plus .includes, an || chain or a switch would have passed. FIXED in this session: the scan now asserts that neither consumer NAMES any canonical member at all, which is strictly stronger and construct-independent; mutation-tested with an array-literal copy, which it caught (102/103). REMAINING and accepted: only the security consumer is pinned by behaviour, so a change to FailureEvidenceCollector.ts:278 that consulted a different list while keeping the alias would still pass section 12.

6 (non-blocking, correct as-is): Recorder and Runner are unaffected, and the four other enumerations are deliberately NOT consolidated — BrowserIsolationResolver.ts:58 and WorkloadWeights.ts:27 enumerate browser-SWAP node types, StepSafetyPolicy.ts:38 is a wider local-session safety class, StepExecutor.ts:794 is a page-restoration exclusion. Folding any of them onto the protected-login set would couple unrelated policies and would be the real defect. Pre-existing and out of scope: the two BROWSER_SWAP_NODE_TYPES copies duplicate each other.

7 (non-blocking, ACTED ON): the failure-evidence evidence note overclaimed — that suite never exercises the suppression path. CORRECTED on this contract, and verify:ui-error-evidence (85/85, section 11) added as the suite that does.

completion.note: Committed as ONE atomic change across two commits because it spans four ownership domains while the lease guard can only commit a single-lease or zero-protected-path index: 2202e933 carries the runner/profile/guard/doc half unleased, 9fc159a8 carries the protected AiAutonomyPolicy half under this contract's security lease. Section 12 of verify:flow-fragments is transiently red at 2202e933 by design and green again at 9fc159a8.
